references.text: The same offerings were given by Nahshon, son of Amminadab, from the tribe of Judah. This shows the standardized pattern for the tribal leaders' offerings.
Nethanel, son of Zuar, from the tribe of Issachar gave identical offerings, confirming the similarity between all the tribes' gifts.
The bowls and dishes of pure gold made for the tabernacle show the background for the holy vessels used in worship.
A grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil was part of the daily sacrifice, here given as a dedication gift.
The instructions for the grain offering describe fine flour mixed with oil, corresponding to the contents of the silver bowls.
The shekel of the sanctuary is mentioned as the standard weight, the same unit of measurement used here to weigh the silver vessels.
